newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai authorities move to calm quake rumors.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai authorities move to calm quake rumors.

text.p: Shanghai's official media on Wednesday urged residents to ignore widespread rumours that a major earthquake was about to strike the city.
The official Liberation Daily said the fears had been encouraged by the thick fog that has enveloped Shanghai on many days recently.

"Some rumors have given the exact time and place for this supposed earthquake, and say that the fog is an omen. This is unscientific," the newspaper quoted the head of Shanghai's Earthquake Bureau, Huo Enjie, as saying.
"In China, the right to announce earthquake predictions belongs to the government alone," he added.
Shanghai, where earthquakes are almost unknown, was slightly shaken in November 1996 by a quake measuring 6.1 on the Richter scale. Its epicentre was in the Yellow Sea east of Shanghai.
The newspaper said aftershock activity from the November earthquake was normal and people should not be concerned.
Two earthquakes measuring 6.4 and 6.3 on the Richter scale hit China's western province of Xinjiang within a minute of each other on Tuesday, killing 12 people and injuring 27.
